tier_reason: Founder decision 2026-09-03: deprioritized alongside angular. Neither Chatwoot nor Intercom -- the closest comparable competitors at Erghi's stage -- maintain framework wrappers around their vanilla widget. Kept as real, working, tested code; not getting further active build investment. Bug fixes and security issues still land.
verification_method: Read react/src/*.ts(x) directly. react/package.json depends on @erghi-ai/sdk ^1.0.0 (react/package.json:30) and useAuth/useChat/useWebSocket call straight into that client's .auth/.chat resources (react/src/useChat.ts:3,17,58,74) rather than reimplementing HTTP calls -- so its *effective* capability ceiling equals whatever javascript/parity.json declares, even though only a curated subset is exposed via hooks today.

auth.evidence: react/src/useAuth.ts wraps client.auth.{login,register,refresh,logout,me}; no hook yet for forgotPassword/resetPassword/verifyEmail even though the underlying client (client.auth.*) already has them -- a hook-surface gap, not a wire-protocol gap.

chat.evidence: react/src/useChat.ts:17,58,74 -- useChat only covers an existing conversation (getMessages/sendMessage/sendTyping); conversation lifecycle (create/list/close) has no hook, callers must reach into client.chat.* directly via useErghi().

notes: This package is structurally a DX layer, not an independent client -- it cannot silently drift on wire format/auth/tenancy the way angular can, because it has no HTTP code of its own. Its only realistic drift risk is 'javascript SDK gained a capability and no hook was added for it' (see auth.password_reset/email_verification and chat.create/list/close above), which is a low-cost, non-urgent gap to close later precisely because a caller can already reach the full client via useErghi().client.*  in the meantime.
